title: Mellow's Lost Bell
markdown:
The sun, a soft warm smile in the sky, sprinkled gentle golden light on the Lullaby Peaks. Tilly Cloud, a kind young witch with hair the colour of moonbeams and bright curious eyes that sparkled like little stars, hummed a quiet happy tune as she wandered along the familiar paths. Beside her, Mellow, her plump and friendly marmot whose fur was the warm comforting colour of honey, waddled along with a gentle rhythm, his whiskers twitching with every soft step.

Mellow paused, his little pink nose wiggling as if sniffing a secret. He let out a tiny soft sigh. His soft brown eyes grew a little wider. His furry ears drooped just a little, like little wilting petals.

“My borrowed bell!” he whispered. His usually cheerful face clouded over, and a tiny tremble went through his whiskers. “I completely forgot to return Mrs. Whispering Willow’s lovely bell!”

The borrowed bell, the borrowed bell, back to the willow we go.

Tilly smiled, her eyes twinkling with understanding. “Don’t you worry, Mellow. We will take it right back to her. She lives near the bendy Whispering Willow, doesn’t she? The one with the leaves that always seem to be telling secrets?”

Mellow nodded, a little more bravely now. And so, hand in paw, they wandered along, their little mission clear and the gentle sunshine warming their backs.

They walked into the softly echoing pine wood, where tall ancient trees reached for the sky like sleepy giants stretching their arms. The air smelled of warm pine needles and the cool damp earth. As they rounded a mossy fallen log that looked like a sleepy brown bear, they met Pipkin. Pipkin was a neat little goblin, no taller than a toadstool, with round spectacles perched wobbly on his nose and a wonderfully worn satchel overflowing with rolled-up maps. He was carefully drawing a wobbly delightful line on a large green leaf, his brow furrowed in concentration.

“Hello there!” chirped Pipkin, looking up with bright curious eyes. “Are you perhaps looking for a specific spot? I make maps of these lovely parts, you see. All the twisty trails and quiet clearings!”

Tilly explained Mellow’s little predicament with the borrowed bell. Pipkin’s round face lit up with an eager helpful smile. “Ah, the Whispering Willow! I know just the way to her clearing. It’s my favourite place for a quiet moment. Follow me, please!”

He unfurled a map from his satchel, a wonderful picture of wiggly lines, cheerful dots, and little drawings of friendly flowers. He pointed a small knobbly finger. “This way, through the twisty turny path, then a little skip over the smooth flat stones, and you’ll be there in a jiffy. It’s a lovely shortcut, I promise!”

The borrowed bell, the borrowed bell, back to the willow we go.

They eagerly followed Pipkin along a path that wound and twirled like a happy playful snake through the dappled sunlight. It was a truly lovely path, full of funny-shaped stones that looked like sleeping animals and clusters of little bluebell flowers that seemed to nod a cheerful hello. Mellow felt a little flutter in his tummy, a tiny worry about the bell, but he tried to focus on the pretty flowers. For a moment he chased a flitting butterfly, so delighted by its painted wings that he forgot all about the path ahead.

Suddenly he realized the trees looked different. Mellow’s little ears began to droop again, like tiny sad flags. “Oh, dear,” he murmured. “This doesn’t look like the Whispering Willow’s clearing at all. The trees are different here.”

Pipkin peered at his map, his brow furrowed. Then he peered at the surrounding trees, then back at his map, his spectacles sliding down his nose. “Oh, my,” he said, his voice growing a little smaller. “I think… I think we might have taken a little detour. This path actually leads to the Giggling Gorge, not the peaceful Whispering Willow.” His shoulders slumped. “I am terribly sorry. I got a little bit muddled with the twists and turns.”

Tilly remained calm. She gave Mellow a gentle comforting pat. “It’s alright, Mellow. Pipkin was trying his very best to help us. Look at all these pretty wild flowers we’ve discovered.”

Pipkin looked very sorry indeed. Tilly’s warm smile stayed kind. “It’s quite alright, Pipkin. You were trying to help. Perhaps we can find the way together now?”

Pipkin’s worried face brightened. He smoothed out his map again, his fingers tracing the lines with renewed determination. “Yes! Let me just look properly this time. If we go back just a little way, past that big round boulder that looks like a sleepy giant’s belly… yes! And then we turn towards the tallest pine tree with the friendly-looking knot that looks like a smiling face… ah! That should lead us right there.”

And so, with Pipkin carefully guiding them, pointing out each landmark with care, and Tilly keeping a steady calm, they found the correct path. It was a gentle winding path, lined with the softest green moss and delicate little ferns that unfurled like tiny green scrolls. The sun, now lower in the sky, was painting the fluffy clouds in rosy pink and soft warm orange. Soon they could hear the gentle rustle of leaves that sounded remarkably like soft friendly whispers. Bluebells nodded. Their petals were a velvety soft blue. They smelled sweet like honey, and a gentle hum came from the tiny bees that danced among them.

There, by a little bubbling stream that sang a quiet cheerful song, stood the Whispering Willow, her long graceful branches swaying gently in the evening air. And there, sitting peacefully near her mossy roots, was Mrs. Whispering Willow, her wise old face looking rather patient and kind. Mellow, holding the little silver bell carefully in his paws, scurried forward with a happy wiggle.

“Oh, Mrs. Willow! I am so very sorry I borrowed your lovely bell for so long! I quite forgot to bring it back! Here it is!”

He placed the small silver bell gently on the soft mossy ground, where it gleamed softly in the fading light.

Mrs. Whispering Willow’s leaves rustled kindly. “Thank you, Mellow dear. It is a very pretty bell, and I was happy to lend it to you. But I am indeed happy to have it back. And thank you, Tilly, for bringing him along safely and kindly.”

As the last sliver of the sun dipped below the Lullaby Peaks, Tilly, Mellow, and Pipkin waved goodbye. Pipkin tucked his map away with a satisfied smile. Tilly and Mellow walked home, their path now softly illuminated by silvery moonlight. Mellow’s tummy felt still. The worry had gone. The borrowed bell stayed with the willow, where it belonged.

The borrowed bell, the borrowed bell, home with the willow it stays.
characters: Mellow (honey-furred marmot), Tilly Cloud (moonbeam-haired young witch)
